headline: Mother reunited with 8-year-old who climbed trees to survive Nepal floods
summary: After days of frantic searching and fearing both her children were lost, a mother was reunited with her 8-year-old son, Zoyal Ghale, who survived Nepal's devastating floods by climbing trees.
details: Zoyal Ghale, an 8-year-old boy, was joyfully reunited with his mother, Matti Maya Tamang, after surviving Nepal's deadly floods by running into a forest and climbing trees. He was airlifted from the devastated Rasuwa district with a broken leg and facial cuts, while his mother desperately searched for him and his brother.

Tamang had visited multiple shelters and collection points, finding no trace of her children and had begun to accept they were no more. Her immense relief came after a Reuters journalist helped connect her with Zoyal, who had been transferred to a Kathmandu hospital.

The floods were triggered by a glacier collapse near the Langtang Lirung mountain peak, causing an avalanche and massive landslide that swept through valleys. Within minutes, entire communities were leveled, and Zoyal's school building was destroyed.

Zoyal recounted running from his school into the forest with a friend and climbing trees when the flood struck, recalling the sudden darkness. He was later rescued by police officers who gave him money to persuade him to go to the hospital for treatment.

UNICEF reports that at least 17,000 children have been affected by the floods across Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading districts. So far, at least 580 people have been confirmed dead and around 2,500 are still missing in Nepal and China's Tibet.

A Reuters journalist, Sahana Bajracharya, met Ghale at a small hospital and, after hearing about his plight, helped facilitate the reunion. She left her contact at the hospital, and Tamang called her hours later, arranging transport for the mother to reach Kathmandu.

Zoyal's father, a construction laborer in Japan, is also on his way to join them. Despite the widespread devastation, Tamang found a degree of normality, remarking on Zoyal's mischievous nature and previous broken bones.

headline_marked: [[Polao rice price doubles]] in Bangladesh, hitting record highs; farmers see no benefit
headline: Polao rice price doubles in Bangladesh, hitting record highs; farmers see no benefit
summary: The price of polao rice has surged by 100% in six months, reaching unprecedented levels. While traders attribute the hike to exports, farmers who sold their paddy at lower rates are not benefiting from the current high prices.
details: In Rajshahi, the price of polao rice has doubled in the last six months, with traders stating they have never witnessed such a drastic increase. What once cost BDT 100 per kg now sells for BDT 200-230.

Farmers, however, report selling their paddy at nearly half the current market price during the production season. By the time prices soared, most farmers had already sold their stock, preventing them from benefiting from the price surge.
Many farmers and traders believe increased exports are the primary reason for the price hike. Three leading companies collectively exported 1,530 metric tons of rice in the 2025-26 fiscal year.

Polao rice is primarily made from BRRI-34 (Chinigura) paddy, with most of it produced in Dinajpur, along with Thakurgaon and Panchagarh. Dinajpur aimed to produce paddy on 260,860 hectares this year, with Chinigura cultivated on 95,000 hectares.

Several large companies, including Square Food & Beverage, Ispahani Agro, and Pran Agro, package and market aromatic rice made from Chinigura paddy. Dinajpur alone has nearly 200 auto rice mills processing this variety.

Consumers express shock at the sudden price jump. One buyer in Rajshahi noted paying BDT 230 per kg recently, up from BDT 140 five months prior, while a restaurant owner now buys at BDT 200 per kg, compared to BDT 130 six months ago.

Wholesale rice traders in Rajshahi are selling polao rice for BDT 180-200 per kg, with retail prices even higher. They unanimously state that prices began rising after Eid-ul-Adha, increasing by about BDT 100 per kg.

A wholesale trader in Rajshahi was fined BDT 10,000 by the Directorate of National Consumer Rights Protection for selling polao rice at BDT 200 per kg. He explained that he buys from company warehouses at that price, adding only a 10-20% commission.

Farmers like Khaledul Islam from Dinajpur sold a 75 kg sack of Chinigura paddy for BDT 4,000-5,200 last season. The price later rose to BDT 5,200, but by then, farmers had no stock left. Another farmer, Habibur Rahman, increased his Chinigura cultivation this year due to rising prices.
